questions.stem: How does smoking increase the risk of cardiovascular disease?

options.text: It causes the heart to grow larger over time
It damages artery walls, promoting atherosclerosis and blood clot formation
It reduces the number of white blood cells in the blood
It increases the amount of plasma in the blood

questions.explanation: Chemicals in cigarette smoke damage the endothelium (inner lining) of artery walls, making it easier for fatty deposits to build up. Smoking also makes blood more likely to clot, increasing the risk of heart attacks and strokes.
